chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Sabah, saying: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, saying: He who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

When the Qa'im (peace be upon him) appears, those who thought themselves to be of his people will depart from this matter, and those who are like the worshippers of the sun and the moon will enter into it.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Mahdi (peace be upon him)
key_terms.شُبْهُ عُبَّادِ الشَّمْسِ وَالْقَمَرِ: Those resembling the worshippers of the sun and the moon (a metaphor for a specific group of believers or apostates)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the followers of the Mahdi when he appears?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the phenomenon of 'false claimants' who, driven by political ambition rather than genuine faith, will seize power during the Mahdi's era, mirroring the pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah practice of astral worship. This serves as a critical test for the Shia, distinguishing true believers from those who merely seek worldly dominance under the guise of religious authority.
